## 2. Check prices with no account 

```
curl -sL https://lium.io/pricing.json | jq -r '.models[]
  | select(.available_gpus > 0)
  | "\(.name)  from $\(.min_price_usd_per_gpu_hour)/GPU-hour  \(.available_gpus) free"'

```

At 02:44 UTC on 24 September 2026 that printed, among others: H100 80GB HBM3 from $1.30 per GPU-hour, H200 from $3.00, B200 from $5.60, B300 from $8.25, RTX 5090 from $0.58 and RTX 4090 from $0.45. Providers set their own prices, so run it again for the current numbers, or see lium.io/pricing. For one row per rentable node, read the public nodes feed.

...

Billing is per second at the node's hourly price, from deploy until the pod is removed, with no minimum. Ten minutes of an H100 at $1.30 per GPU-hour costs $0.22.

results.title: Renting an 8x B300 by the hour: what it costs and how to start - DEV Community
results.author: Lium
highlights:
Posted on Sep 24 

# Renting an 8x B300 by the hour: what it costs and how to start 

Posted by the Lium team. Lium is the GPU marketplace used in this post. Every number links to a public source you can check yourself.

Video (24 s, play the MP4): one command for 8x B300. The prices on screen were live on lium.io at 02:29 UTC on 24 September 2026.

An 8x B300 node has 2,304 GB of GPU memory (288 GB per card, per Lium's price feed). That is enough to hold very large models on one machine. This post covers three things: what is on the market right now, what an hour costs to the cent, and the commands that take you from nothing to a running 8-GPU pod.

## What is free right now 

Lium publishes two unauthenticated feeds: `pricing.json`, one row per GPU model, and the public nodes feed, one row per rentable node. I read both at 06:05 UTC on 24 September 2026 (nodes feed `generated_at` 06:04:46Z). These are the whole 8-GPU hosts that were free at that minute:

| GPU | Free 8x hosts | Price per GPU-hour |
| --- | --- | --- |
| B300 | 4 | $8.50–$9.50 |
| B200 | 0 | – |
| H200 | 1 | $4.00 |
| H100 80GB HBM3 | 3 | $1.90–$2.75 |
| A100-SXM4-80GB | 5 | $1.10–$1.23 |

On the same read, single GPUs were free too: 38 B300 at $8.25–$9.50, 4 B200 at $5.50–$6.50, 15 H200 at $3.00–$4.00, 42 H100 at $1.30–$2.75 and 41 A100 80GB at $0.999–$1.23.

Video (23 s, play the MP4): the lowest live ask for ten GPU models, from one curl. Its prices are from 02:29 UTC; the table above is the later 06:05 UTC read.

Providers set their own prices, so these numbers move. The feed is rebuilt at most once a minute (docs). This one-liner prints every free 8-GPU host of these five models when you read this: 

```
curl -sS https://lium.io/api/public/v1/nodes | jq -c '.nodes[]
  | select((.gpu_model | test("B300|B200|H200|H100|A100")) and .available_gpu_count >= 8)
  | {gpu_model, available_gpu_count, price_per_gpu_hour, reliability_score, country_code}'

```

## What it costs 

Lium bills per second at the listed hourly price: a pod costs `hourly price × seconds / 3600` for the exact seconds it exists, with no minimum (billing docs). At $8.50 per GPU-hour, the lowest 8x B300 ask on this read, an 8x B300 pod costs $68.00 per hour:

| Pod lifetime | Cost for 8x B300 at $8.50/GPU-hour |
| --- | --- |
| 20 seconds (a smoke test that fails fast) | $0.38 |
| 1 minute | $1.13 |
| 10 minutes | $11.33 |
| 1 hour | $68.00 |

...

Current prices per model are on lium.io/pricing, and the B300 page is lium.io/gpu/b300-sxm6-ac.

Updated 24 September 2026, 06:05 UTC: fresh price read, and a video of a real 8x B300 rental.

results.author: TransAtlas Editorial
highlights:
Every number in this ranking comes from the TransAtlas live price database, collected on 2026-10-23 at 22:11 UTC: 410 listings across 10 GPU-specialized platforms. If you want the conclusion before the ranking, compare all cloud GPU providers for a side-by-side table of per-GPU-hour rates, spot discounts and egress fees. Here is exactly how the ranking was built, so you can reproduce or challenge it:

...

## 1 Lium: The Marketplace With the Widest Catalog

Lium lists 92 distinct GPU models: everything from a GTX 1060 to an H800 PCIe: which is why it tops the breadth index. Its verified prices are genuinely aggressive where stock exists: RTX A6000 at $0.42/GPU-h (the cheapest in our dataset), H200 Spot at $3.85, and B200 at $5.50 on-demand. Two caveats keep it from being an unconditional recommendation: only 25% of its listings were rentable at collection time, and our parser completeness for Lium is low: treat its catalog as a hunting ground, not an SLA. Best for batch jobs and researchers who can shop around and tolerate churn.

results.title: Lium Tops LocalMaxxing Qwen3.6 35B Board With 14,499 Tokens Per Second
results.author: Tristan Hillerich
highlights: Lium calculated the run at $0.107 per million output tokens, based on a listed B200 rental price of $5.60 per hour and 52.2 million output tokens per hour. The team compared that with $0.90 per million tokens for the cheapest FP8 OpenRouter provider it cited for the same model, and said the result points to a lower-cost path for high-throughput open-model inference.

results.title: Lium - the Startup Already Reshaping the GPU Market | Hashrate
highlights: Lium is a GPU marketplace built by Datura AI. It launched in late 2024 as Celium and became Lium in mid-2025. Instead of one company owning every card, independent providers around the world list their own hardware, and anyone can rent high-performance GPUs from that pool on demand. The catalog is wide: 21 different GPU models were rented in August 2026 alone, spanning everything from RTX 4090s up to H100, H200, B200, and B300 cards. Each provider sets its own hourly price, and billing runs per second at that rate, with no minimum, so a renter never pays for idle time between jobs.

results.title: Nebius raises GPU prices again October 1; H100 to $4.50, B300 to $9.50 | GPU Cloud Advisors
highlights:
# Nebius raises GPU prices again October 1; H100 to $4.50, B300 to $9.50

Nebius lists higher on demand GPU prices effective October 1, 2026. H100 rises from $3.85 to $4.50 per GPU hour. H200 rises from $4.50 to $5.40, B200 from $7.15 to $8.50, and B300 from $7.85 to $9.50. This round is 17% to 21%. It is reported to be the second increase since May. [1] [2]

Published September 28, 2026 Announced, effective October 1, 2026

## Disclosed terms

HGX H100, per GPU hour

$3.85 now, $4.50 from October 1 [1]

HGX H200, per GPU hour

$4.50 now, $5.40 from October 1 [1]

HGX B200, per GPU hour

$7.15 now, $8.50 from October 1 [1]

HGX B300, per GPU hour

$7.85 now, $9.50 from October 1 [1]

...

### What changed

Nebius's pricing page now shows two on demand columns: today's rate and a rate effective October 1, 2026. H100 rises 17%, H200 20%, B200 19% and B300 21%. [1]

Spot rates still start at $0.79 for H100 and H200 and $0.99 for B200 and B300. RTX PRO 6000 stays at $1.80. CPU only instances also rise. Nebius still advertises commitment discounts of up to 35% off on demand for multi month cluster reservations. [1]

Nebius's pricing page does not give a reason for the change.

...

The Motley Fool reports that in early May, Nebius's pricing page showed H100 at $2.95 per hour and B300 at $6.10.

...

H100: At $4.50, Nebius moves above Runpod ($3.49), Crusoe ($3.90) and Lambda ($4.29). It stays below CoreWeave's 8 GPU instance, about $6.16 per GPU.

H200: At $5.40, Nebius moves above Runpod ($4.59) and Verda ($4.55). It stays below Together AI ($5.99) and CoreWeave (about $6.31 per GPU).

B200: At $8.50, Nebius moves well above Lambda ($6.69) and Runpod ($6.79). CoreWeave's 8 GPU instance works out to about $8.60 per GPU.

B300: At $9.50, Nebius moves above Verda ($8.20) and Scaleway ($7.50). Together AI lists $9.99.

Configurations differ. vCPUs, memory, storage, networking and minimum allocation all vary. A lower hourly rate is not a lower project cost on its own.

...

Ask Nebius whether a commitment signed before October 1 is priced at the current rate.

...

If you run on Nebius on demand today, your bill goes up October 1 unless your contract says otherwise. Check whether your agreement fixes the rate.

If you have a Nebius quote in hand, ask which rate it uses. A quote issued in September may still show the old price.

results.title: Nebius to increase prices for Nvidia GPU resources from October By Investing.com
highlights:
Investing.com -- Nebius will raise prices for its on-demand GPU services starting Oct. 1, the company said in an emailed statement, according to Bloomberg News. 

The price increases will apply to Nvidia H100, H200, B200 and B300 GPU resources, according to the statement. The company will also raise rates for certain CPU and memory resources.

The new pricing structure takes effect at the beginning of next month.

results.title: Nebius to Increase GPU Rental Prices by Up to 21% Starting October 1 | KuCoin
Nebius Said to Raise Prices for its On-demand Compute Resources Starting October | MemoryMarket - memory prices, market analysis, industry news, research report
results.author: By: M
highlights:
By: M 2026-09-17 09:31 (UTC+0) 

According to media reports, Nebius will raise prices for some of its on-demand computing resources starting October 1, marking the company's second round of price increases since May. Under the new pricing plan, the price of H100 will rise from $3.85 per GPU hour to $4.50, an increase of about 17%; H200 will rise 20% from $4.50 to $5.40; B200 will rise nearly 19% from $7.15 to $8.50; and B300 will rise about 21% from $7.85 per GPU hour to $9.50. The changes also extend to CPU-only compute. AMD EPYC Genoa CPU rates will rise 25% to $0.015 per vCPU-hour from $0.012, while Genoa memory will increase about 41% to $0.0045 per GiB-hour from $0.0032. The ultimate impact on customers' bills will therefore depend on their configurations and usage.
